newsitem.title: USA: Covance CEO says co to "fare well" alone.
newsitem.headline: Covance CEO says co to "fare well" alone.

text.p: Covance Inc begins its first day of regular way trading on Tuesday, and President and Chief Executive Officer Christopher Kuebler expects the company to "fare very well" since its spinoff from Corning Inc.
"We're in an outstanding industry," Kuebler told Reuters on Tuesday, "We think we'll fare very well."
Covance shares closed Monday at 19-7/8 in when-issued trading on the New York Stock Exchange.

Kuebler said Covance's position as a provider of integrated product development services on a worldwide basis to the biotechnology, pharmaceutical and medical device industries will help it do well in the growing outsourcing business.
He said companies are moving to outsourcing as speed becomes essential for releasing drug products.
Covance was part of Corning for 10 years, but Kuebler said the break from the parent company was necessary.
"We will be valued to a much greater extent outside of Corning," he said, adding that Corning's core business is glass and technology.
Kuebler said Covance's major business segments include pre-clinical testing, human clinical testing, pharmaceutical research packaging and biological manufacturing.

Covance also provides some services such as health economics for managed care organizations, hospitals and health care provider networks, as well as early development and laboratory testing services to the chemical, agrochemical and food industries.
He said the company works with hundreds of providers and the top 50 pharmaceutical companies are clients.
Covance is looking at three or four approaches for growth, Kuebler said, including geographic expansion into Latin America.
The company just recently expanded into Singapore, he said.

Covance now deals mostly with the pharmaceutical and biological industries but is looking to increase its clientele by expanding services to healthcare providers and government organizations, Kuebler said.
Corning Inc on January 2 announced the completion of its spinoff of Covance, formerly known as Corning Pharmaceuticals Services, to its shareholders of record on December 31.
Corning distributed one Covance share for every four Corning shares.

Covance reported net revenues of $357 million and net income of $25 million for the nine months ended September 30, compared with net revenues of $303 million and net income $18.5 million for the year-earlier period.
Net income results for the 1995 period excludes the impact of a second quarter 1995 restructuring charge.
Quest Diagnostics Inc, formerly known as Corning Clinical Laboratories Inc, is also beginning its first day of regular way trading Tuesday since its spinoff from Corning.
Quest shares closed at 16-1/4 on Monday in when-issued trading on the NYSE.
-- Mona Ghuneim, New York News Desk, 212-859-1700
